fluff.overview:
The Shadow Cat II is a sixty-ton Clan BattleMech developed by Clan Jade Falcon during the waning years of the Jihad. Rather than invest time in an entirely new design, the Falcons chose to build upon proven technology by scaling up the successful Shadow Cat OmniMech, adding fifteen tons in the manner of other successful Clan II designs such as the Ryoken II and Mad Cat Mk II. The design originated from an unfinished Homeworld prototype completed by Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten at the direction of a merchant who recognized the opportunity to leverage existing production infrastructure.

The Shadow Cat II served as the Jade Falcons' primary testbed for hyper-assault Gauss rifle technology, which they had won exclusive production rights to through Trials. Production has remained exclusively at the Olivetti Weaponry facility on Sudeten since the design's introduction in 3076, and access to the design has been closely guarded by the Falcons against all attempts at acquisition.
fluff.capabilities:
The Shadow Cat II employs the same weight-saving technologies as its lighter predecessor, utilizing a Type 79-60 endo steel internal structure and a Type 79 360 XL extralight engine to achieve a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour despite its increased mass. Clan Standard Type A1 jump jets provide a 180-meter jumping capability, granting mobility that belies the 'Mech's heavy weight classification. Seven and a half tons of Compound H17 ferro-fibrous armor offer only marginally more protection than the lighter Shadow Cat, a deliberate trade-off that prioritizes speed and firepower over survivability.

The Shadow Cat II's primary weapon is a right-arm Type 0 Hyper-Assault Gauss 20, a devastating weapon that unleashes a spread of projectiles capable of stripping nearly two full tons of armor in a single volley. Twin Type X Short Bow LRM-10 launchers mounted in each torso extend the engagement envelope, while a Series 7Ja ER medium laser in the right torso provides minimal ammo-independent backup. The shotgun-like damage pattern of the HAG makes the Shadow Cat II exceptionally effective at exploiting already-damaged opponents, though it struggles to focus damage against heavily armored, pristine targets.
fluff.history:
Since its introduction in 3076, the Shadow Cat II has been deployed almost exclusively by Clan Jade Falcon. The design's origins during the Jihad era reflected the Falcons' pragmatic approach to military procurement, favoring rapid development and proven technology over lengthy design cycles. The Olivetti Weaponry facility on Sudeten has served as the sole production site throughout the design's service life, with the facility's long history of Falcon control providing a stable manufacturing base.

The Jade Falcons have guarded access to the Shadow Cat II jealously. No other Inner Sphere Clan successfully won a Trial of Possession for the design during the Republic era, and Republic Intelligence noted that while the Diamond Sharks attempted to acquire production rights through trade agreements, these efforts were consistently rebuffed. This exclusivity has kept the Shadow Cat II relatively rare compared to other Clan heavy designs, but it has earned a fearsome reputation within Falcon formations.

Despite its limited distribution, the Shadow Cat II has proven itself a capable fire support platform. Its combination of speed, jumping ability, and ranged firepower allows it to maintain favorable engagement distances while supporting heavier assault elements. The introduction of several variants throughout the late Jihad and Dark Age eras demonstrates the Falcons' continued investment in the design, with each new variant exploring different tactical applications for the versatile chassis.
fluff.deployment: Introduced in 3092 during the Dark Age, the Shadow Cat II 4 returns to the design's fire support roots with a loadout centered on a Gauss rifle and paired LRM-10 launchers. This configuration recalls the original prototype's planned Gauss rifle armament that was abandoned in favor of HAG technology during development. The trade-off comes in reduced mobility, as the removal of one jump jet limits jump capability to 150 meters. This variant offers more focused, precise long-range firepower compared to the base model's area-denial approach.
